channel.title: News Today — Smart AI News Portal
channel.description: বাংলাদেশ, ভারত ও বিশ্বের সর্বশেষ খবর — স্বয়ংক্রিয়ভাবে আপডেটেড

item.title: Adam Mosseri Warns Public Backlash Against AI Will Intensify
item.description: During a podcast interview, Instagram chief Adam Mosseri stated that public hostility toward artificial intelligence is widespread and expected to grow. He noted that the aversion extends far beyond students and artists.

item.title: Jio Platforms Debuts as India's Second Most Valuable Firm
item.description: Jio Platforms launched on the stock exchange with a share price of Rs 1,358, eventually climbing to Rs 1,419. This initial trading value pushed its market capitalization to Rs 13.1 lakh crore, making it India's second most valuable company.

item.title: পরিবারকে নামাজের প্রতি উদ্বুদ্ধ করার ইসলামী নির্দেশনা
item.description: পবিত্র কোরআনের নির্দেশনা অনুযায়ী নিজের পাশাপাশি পরিবারকে নিয়মিত নামাজ আদায়ে উদ্বুদ্ধ করা এবং এর ওপর অবিচল থাকা আবশ্যক। সুরা ত্বহার ১৩২ নম্বর আয়াতে এ বিষয়ে স্পষ্টভাবে তাগিদ দেওয়া হয়েছে।

item.title: Fully Upgraded Touchscreen MacBook Pro Reaches High Cost
item.description: Purchasing Apple's new touchscreen MacBook Pro with all available hardware upgrades will cost consumers approximately $14,549, setting a new high for laptop pricing.

item.title: Supreme Court Issues Contempt Summons to Sanjay Raut
item.description: The Supreme Court has issued a formal summons to Sanjay Raut in connection with an ongoing contempt of court proceeding.

item.title: Australian Politics: Man Cautioned for Stalking MPs and Gas Vote
item.description: Australian authorities issued a caution to a man accused of stalking female Labor MPs. Meanwhile, the lower house is scheduled to debate and vote on domestic gas reservation policies.

item.title: FCC Chairman Proposes Allowing Prisons to Block Smuggled Phones
item.description: The Federal Communications Commission will hold a vote next month to potentially soften its historical stance against signal jammers. The move would permit correctional facilities to disable unauthorized mobile devices.

item.title: UN Experts Criticize Police Violence During French Student Protests
item.description: United Nations experts have criticized law enforcement methods used against student demonstrators in France. They warned that these heavy-handed crackdowns discourage citizens from peacefully exercising their rights.

item.title: Fleetwood Town draws Everton or Newcastle in EFL Cup
item.description: In the EFL Cup quarter-finals, League Two club Fleetwood Town will host either Everton or Newcastle United at Highbury Stadium.

item.title: Supreme Court has not yet evaluated SIR logical discrepancy
item.description: The Supreme Court stated it has not yet examined the legality surrounding logical discrepancies within the SIR.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro denies leaving Brazil following Miami arrival
item.description: After arriving in Miami, the defeated Brazilian politician rejected claims he fled the country, alleging political persecution.

item.title: Hack exposes data of over 41,000 US immigration workers
item.description: A cyberattack carried out by a group named the Department of Peace leaked records concerning more than 41,000 DHS employees.

item.title: Young girl suffers severe injuries in German wolf attack
item.description: An eight-year-old child was seriously hurt by a wolf while inside an enclosure at a German wildlife park alongside staff.

item.title: NHS Western Isles leads Scotland in weight loss drug prescriptions
item.description: A report highlights major differences among Scottish health boards, with NHS Western Isles prescribing weight loss medications at triple the average rate.

item.title: British historian gives 50 colonial Indian artworks to Tate
item.description: British art historian Charles Greig has donated 50 colonial-era Indian paintings by European and Indian artists to Tate London.

item.title: Russo hat-trick leads Arsenal past Benfica in Champions League
item.description: Alessia Russo scored three goals in Arsenal's 3-0 victory against Benfica, becoming England's top scorer in the Women's Champions League.

item.title: Texas barber turns in cash found at ATM
item.description: A Texas barber facing a rent shortage discovered two bags containing $128,514 at an ATM in Lewisville. Despite his own financial struggles, he handed the money over to law enforcement. The funds belonged to a Brink's security team.

item.title: Georgia appeals court rules on guardianship case
item.description: The Georgia Court of Appeals resolved a family dispute regarding the care of a 95-year-old woman with advanced dementia. Siblings had disagreed over visitation rights and financial management following actions by one of the sons.

item.title: NDA secures sixteen seats in legislative elections
item.description: The NDA captured sixteen out of twenty-eight available seats during the MLC elections. Meanwhile, the Congress party experienced a setback in the voting results.

item.title: Actress Barbara Barrie dies at 95 in New York
item.description: Veteran stage and screen actress Barbara Barrie passed away in New York City at the age of 95 through a medically assisted death. Her daughter confirmed the death of the Oscar-nominated performer known for her work in film and Broadway.

item.title: Political clash over Tata and economy
item.description: Opposition leader Rahul criticized the administration regarding the Tata group, prompting a direct response from Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman. The exchange highlighted ongoing political tensions over economic matters.

item.title: Microsoft discloses Azure quarterly revenue figure
item.description: Microsoft has publicly revealed the exact quarterly revenue for its Azure cloud division at $33.2 billion. This disclosure provides a clear look at its financial standing relative to top competitors in the cloud market.

item.title: FedEx exceeds financial forecasts for the quarter
item.description: FedEx surpassed Wall Street's third-quarter expectations for both revenue and earnings. The company also adjusted its fiscal outlook upward following the recent calendar shifts.

item.title: Christopher Lloyd reflects on his Connecticut upbringing
item.description: Actor Christopher Lloyd, aged 88, shared memories of his youth spent on the 400-acre Waveny estate in Connecticut. His family moved to the property in 1944, which was later purchased by the town of New Canaan to become a public park.

item.title: Spain Train Collision Leaves At Least 68 Dead
item.description: An accident involving a moving train and a stationary one resulted in at least 68 fatalities in Spain. The nation's transport minister attributed the incident to an unexplained mistake.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro Flies to Miami Following Brazil Election Loss
item.description: Right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro boarded a flight to Miami from Ecuador after previously crossing into Argentina following his electoral defeat in Brazil.

item.title: Report: Australian SAS Leaders Aware of Afghan Weapon Planting
item.description: According to an Australian Defence Force inspector, leadership failed to intervene as SAS personnel placed weapons on deceased Afghans. The inquiry cited severe leadership failures behind these actions.

item.title: Data Breach Exposes Over 40,000 DHS Staff Records
item.description: A cyber intruder accessed personal data belonging to over 41,000 Department of Homeland Security personnel. The compromised details include phone numbers, email addresses, job titles, and workplace locations.

item.title: Cisgender Women Challenge Transgender Rights Equality in Supreme Court
item.description: Biological women have submitted arguments at the Supreme Court contesting equal rights for transgender women.

item.title: Google Rolls Out AI Search Advertisements Worldwide
item.description: Alphabet reported a 25% year-over-year revenue increase to $127.6 billion in its third-quarter financial results. Alongside the earnings, the company launched AI-powered search advertisements globally amid slower core ad growth.

item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro Arrives in US and Claims Brazilian Leadership
item.description: Following a runoff election defeat on Sunday, Flavio Bolsonaro traveled to the United States alongside relatives. Despite losing the presidential race, he proclaimed himself the true leader of Brazil.

item.title: Vance Writes to Iranian Official for Talks as Trump Warns of Attacks
item.description: Amid threats of military strikes from Donald Trump, Vance has written to an Iranian hard-liner in an effort to restart diplomatic negotiations.

item.title: Chipotle Stock Climbs 7% on Positive Sales Projections
item.description: Chipotle shares increased by 7% after Chief Executive Scott Boatwright forecasted ongoing growth in same-store sales. He also noted that lower-income patrons surpassed high-income customers at restaurants during the quarter.

item.title: Costa Rica opens $35m maximum-security facility
item.description: Leader Laura Fernandez opened a new $35 million correctional facility close to San Jose designed to hold as many as 5,100 detainees.

item.title: Passengers recount trauma following Spanish rail wreck
item.description: Uninjured yet shaken travelers shared accounts of fear and frustration after Wednesday's railway disaster within Toledo province.

item.title: Microsoft reports $10 billion in earnings from OpenAI
item.description: During the quarter ending September 30, Microsoft generated $10 billion through commercial ties and revenue sharing with OpenAI. This figure highlights the massive monetary reliance within their ongoing collaboration.

item.title: Hayden Panettiere's passing determined accidental by authorities
item.description: The Nashville and Heroes actress passed away in August due to the lethal combination of fentanyl, Xanax, and additional substances, concluding the police investigation.

item.title: Vincent Kompany leaves medical facility after fainting episode
item.description: Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany has left the hospital and is recovering successfully after falling ill at the team's training facility, a club executive stated.

item.title: Transfer updates: Sancho declines Getafe offer
item.description: Unattached player Jadon Sancho has declined a transfer to Spain, Desire Doue discusses a new deal with Paris St-Germain, and Everton eyes Marcus Rashford.

item.title: Indonesian youth protest inflation and wildfire response
item.description: A large group of students in Indonesia demonstrated against official policies concerning environmental blazes and increasing living expenses.

item.title: Akai previews open-source MPC keyboard modification
item.description: Even before its official debut, Akai is highlighting community-driven modifications for the upcoming keyboard-equipped alternative to the standard MPC sampler.

item.title: Microsoft Posts Tenth Successive Quarter of Record Revenue
item.description: Microsoft announced Wednesday that quarterly revenue reached $92.3 billion, marking a 19 percent year-over-year rise and the tenth consecutive quarter of record earnings for the company.

item.title: Spanish Authorities Probe Deadly High-Speed Train Crash
item.description: An official inquiry is underway following a high-speed train collision in Spain on Wednesday that resulted in at least 68 deaths and approximately 100 injuries. This marks the nation's second fatal train disaster within a year.

item.title: EU Drops Proposal for Canadian Associate Membership Talks
item.description: Following internal disputes among member nations, the European Union has withdrawn a proposed invitation for Canada to begin negotiations regarding associate membership, opting instead for a less formal association at the Montreal summit.

item.title: Ford Motor Releases Q3 Financial Results
item.description: Automaker Ford Motor posted third-quarter financial figures that surpassed analyst forecasts for earnings, though revenue fell slightly short of expectations.

item.title: Delhi High Court Dismisses Plea Over NRI Passport Fees
item.description: The Delhi High Court has thrown out a public interest litigation challenging the recent increases in passport fees applicable to non-resident Indians.

item.title: European Gas Costs Exceed €100 Mark Ahead of Winter
item.description: European natural gas rates climbed past €100 per megawatt-hour on Wednesday, reaching a peak not seen since 2022. While the EU maintains that supplies are secure despite storage levels sitting at 72 percent, households face a challenging winter.

item.title: Readwise Expands Digital Reading Services
item.description: Readwise, known for its highlight-management software and the Readwise Reader application, is positioning itself to compete directly with established electronic book platforms like Kindle and Kobo.

item.title: California Siblings Charged Over Unfinished Backyard Dwellings
item.description: Two California brothers who founded Anchored Tiny Homes face 35 felony charges each after failing to build a backyard structure for a retired nurse who paid over $40,000 in 2023. The firm drew upwards of 200 grievances spanning 18 counties for abandoned construction and unreturned funds.

item.title: Uttarakhand forest relocation plan rejected by panel
item.description: A panel has once again dismissed the Uttarakhand High Court's relocation proposal due to forest land issues. The state government must now investigate non-forest sites for the project before seeking any forest clearance.

item.title: Pride and Prejudice series trailer featuring Corrin and Lowden
item.description: A new trailer for the upcoming limited series adaptation of Jane Austen's novel has been released. It highlights the intricate dynamic between Elizabeth Bennet, played by Emma Corrin, and Mr. Darcy, portrayed by Jack Lowden.

item.title: Bolsonaro proclaims himself true Brazilian president from US
item.description: From his base in the United States, Jair Bolsonaro has asserted that he is the legitimate leader of Brazil. He also promised to direct the opposition movement from abroad.

item.title: NCP faction disputes Sunetra Pawar's chief spokesperson pick
item.description: Brijmohan Shrivastav has questioned Sunetra Pawar's authority to name a new national chief spokesperson. He argued that earlier concerns regarding her own national president appointment remain unaddressed.

item.title: বিশ্বব্যাংক: বছরের শেষে পণ্যের দাম ২৩% বাড়তে পারে
item.description: বিশ্বব্যাংক জানিয়েছে, চলতি বছর বৈশ্বিক তেল সরবরাহ ৫.২ শতাংশ এবং ব্যবহার ২.৫ শতাংশ কমতে পারে। এছাড়া বছরের শেষ নাগাদ বিশ্ববাজারে পণ্যের মূল্য ২৩ শতাংশ পর্যন্ত বৃদ্ধি পাওয়ার আশঙ্কা রয়েছে।

item.title: Almost $20m raised to safeguard Queensland land tract
item.description: Nearly $20 million has been secured to acquire the Wooroora station in northern Queensland. Bush Heritage aims to protect this vital ecological corridor, which supports 12 threatened species.

item.title: Chiefs head coach supports kicker Tucker's signing
item.description: Kansas City Chiefs coach Andy Reid has backed the team's choice to add Justin Tucker to the practice squad. Reid pointed out that the kicker has already completed his mandated suspension period.

item.title: 3300-year-old Bronze Age sword found in Italian lake
item.description: Researchers exploring a volcanic crater lake have uncovered multiple ancient artifacts, including intact pottery, a bronze razor, and a Bronze Age sword that remains sharp after millennia.

item.title: Vietnam signs international agreement for cooperative space exploration
item.description: Vietnam has joined the Artemis Accords as the 78th member, committing to principles of transparency and peace in outer space activities. This move aligns the nation with a global framework for responsible lunar and deep-space research.

item.title: Brazilian politician Flavio Bolsonaro relocates to Florida
item.description: Following an unsuccessful election campaign, the prominent political figure has moved to Miami. He was accompanied on the trip by his immediate family members.

item.title: Partial Israeli Vote Tallies Show Netanyahu Bloc Leading
item.description: With 85 percent of votes tallied, Benjamin Netanyahu and his political partners are projected to secure 53 seats within the 120-member parliament, falling short of a full majority.
